data.summary: Follow-up to #147. On yourls.space, the marker "4351361" first appears on 11 Sep, 17 days before #39 was filed, and is reused as "4351361b" in the 30 Sep cluster. A 30 Sep link reads the Airtable view that #80 tied to the SND task, and no further activity appears after 1 Oct.
data.description:
Builds on #147 (Omer Zamir), which links June rmn.re links to Sep 29–Oct 3 probing on yourls.space. #147 leaves one question open: whether the September cluster is the original actor or someone imitating #39 (submitted 28 Sep). The public yourls.space link log, read on 7 Oct 2026, shows earlier activity and a cross-link #147 does not report.

1. The marker is older than #39. On 11 Sep 2026 at 20:44:15 UTC, a link with the keyword 4351361 was created pointing to example.org/createdByChain3627597. On 30 Sep at 11:02:27, the #147 cluster created the keyword 4351361b pointing to example.org/SSRFDESTSP4351361, from a Tencent Cloud address. In YOURLS, a keyword must be unique, so the "b" suffix suggests a reused marker that collided with the 11 Sep link. The 11 Sep creator address belongs to Wowrack, a US hosting range also used by web crawlers. That entry may therefore be a crawler opening a creation link someone had published. Either way, the marker existed 17 days before #39.

2. SSRF test links on 14–15 Sep. Four links created within a minute on 14 Sep (14:53–14:54 UTC) point to 127.0.0.1/admin/, 127.0.0.1:1/, file:///var/www/html/readme.html and an out-of-band callback, 170.106.188.119:9990/ssrf-proof-oob. One more on 15 Sep points to 170.106.188.119:9990/repro-yourlsspace. These are standard tests of whether a shortener will fetch internal or local addresses. The creators were on China Mobile's mobile network (117.136.38.0/24, 223.104.40.0/24). The callback host is registered to Aceville Pte Ltd, Singapore. The naming, "repro" and "ssrf-proof", reads like security testing. Whether this is the #147 actor, a human researcher or someone else is not established.

3. Cross-link to #80. On 30 Sep at 09:57:36, the cluster link my13airgooddirect79318465 reads Airtable shared view viwb5v6acVmfP9fnd. #80 (Laura) records the same view ID as part of the SND task family in May dpaste artifacts. #147 includes this link but redacts its target. This ties the September cluster to a task identifier from May, not only to June's marker style.

4. Activity has stopped. No ag0-family or marker links appear after 1 Oct 04:09. The later entries (1–3 Oct) are the unrelated agentic.report marketing links #147 already excludes.

Bearing on #147's imitation question. The 4351361 marker predates #39, and the Airtable view is a May task identifier. Both make it less likely that the September cluster simply copied #39. They don't rule it out: #80 was also filed on 28 Sep, and the 11 Sep entry may be a crawler hit.

Limits:

Link creation times are taken from the YOURLS log. The 11 Sep creator may be a crawler rather than the actor.
The 14–15 Sep links are not tied to the #147 cluster by any marker. They show SSRF testing on the same shortener two weeks earlier, nothing more.
The Airtable view was not opened. Its signed access had already expired, as #147 notes.
Creator addresses are given to /24, following #147.

Method: Read-only fetch of the public yourls.space statistics API (last 100 links) on 7 Oct 2026, plus public RDAP lookups for the addresses. No links were created or followed.
cyberattack: Other: SSRF test links against shortener software (localhost, file:// and out-of-band callback targets); no confirmed attack.
